The Clinical Pharmacist is responsible for providing comprehensive clinical pharmacy services to ensure the safe, effective, and cost-efficient use of medications. The role collaborates closely with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to optimise medication therapy, improve patient outcomes, and support medication safety and quality initiatives in accordance with organisational policies and regulatory standards. The role is aligned with pharmaceutical care, medication management, and patient safety responsibilities identified within the M42 pharmacy framework.
q: Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) or Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) from an accredited institution.
Current NHRA Pharmacist License or eligibility for licensure.
Minimum 3 to 5 years of clinical pharmacy experience in a hospital or healthcare setting.
Strong knowledge of pharmacotherapy, medication safety, and clinical pharmacy practices
r: li
Review, assess, and optimise medication therapy by evaluating prescriptions for appropriateness, dosage, interactions, contraindications, and therapeutic effectiveness.
li
Participate in multidisciplinary clinical rounds and provide evidence-based medication recommendations to physicians and healthcare teams.
li
Monitor patient response to medication therapy and recommend adjustments to achieve optimal clinical outcomes.
li
Provide medication counselling and education to patients, families, and caregivers regarding medication use, side effects, and adherence.
li
Support medication safety programmes, including adverse drug reaction monitoring, medication error reporting, and risk mitigation initiatives.
li
Develop and implement clinical pharmacy protocols, guidelines, and formulary management activities based on current best practices and evidence-based medicine.
li
Collaborate with healthcare professionals to ensure compliance with medication management standards, accreditation requirements, and regulatory guidelines.
li
Conduct medication reconciliation during admission, transfer, and discharge processes to promote continuity of care.
li
Contribute to quality improvement projects, audits, and clinical research activities related to medication use and patient safety.
li
Provide education and training to healthcare staff, pharmacy interns, and students on medication-related topics and best practices.
li
Maintain accurate clinical documentation and pharmaceutical records in accordance with regulatory and organisational requirements.
li
Promote rational and cost-effective medication use while ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety.

Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the organization’s Early Career strategy and programs, creating structured development pathways that attract, develop, and retain high-potential early-career talent.

The role will oversee graduate, internship, and other early-career development initiatives from program design and selection through onboarding, development, assessment, progression, and program completion. The Manager will work closely with business leaders, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, and external partners to ensure programs build the capabilities and future talent pipelines required by the organization.
The role will also ensure that early-career initiatives provide a high-quality participant experience while delivering measurable business and talent outcomes.

Design structured graduate, internship, trainee, and other early-career development programs.
Define program journeys including onboarding, rotations, formal learning, experiential development, mentoring, assessments, and career progression.
Establish clear program governance, standards, policies, and operating procedures.
Benchmark early-career practices and introduce improvements based on market trends and organizational requirements.
Ensure programs create sustainable pipelines for critical and future capability areas.
Manage early-career programs end to end, from workforce requirements and participant selection through development and graduation.
Build structured development plans and learning journeys for program participants.
Coordinate business rotations, placements, projects, mentoring, coaching, and development activities.
Work with business leaders to identify appropriate placements and meaningful development experiences.
Monitor participant progress and proactively address performance, engagement, or development concerns.
Ensure smooth transitions from early-career programs into permanent roles where applicable.
Establish appropriate assessment methodologies to evaluate participant capability, performance, potential, and development.
Facilitate talent and progress reviews for early-career populations.
Identify high-potential participants and recommend appropriate development and career opportunities.
Partner with Talent Management and Learning & Development teams to address capability gaps.
Use assessment and performance data to continuously improve program design and participant outcomes.

Collaborate with Learning & Development and Leadership Development teams to deliver high-quality development interventions.
Manage relationships with universities, educational institutions, external providers, and development partners where required.
Create a consistent and engaging employee experience throughout the early-career journey.
Develop effective communication and engagement plans for participants and their managers.
Organize development events, networking opportunities, workshops, leadership exposure, and community-building activities.
Establish feedback mechanisms to understand participant experience and identify improvement opportunities.
Act as an escalation point for significant participant or program issues.
Define and monitor KPIs for all Early Career programs.
Track participant performance, retention, engagement, program completion, placement, and progression.
Develop dashboards and reports for Talent Management and HR leadership.
Analyze program data and participant feedback to identify trends and recommend improvements.
Measure program effectiveness and demonstrate the contribution of Early Career initiatives to the organization's future talent pipeline.

Experience partnering with senior business stakeholders and HR Business Partners.
